summary: @servicetitan/datetime-utils preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime tarball from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13, extracts it, chmods the bun binary executable, and then invokes execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js']) at npm install time. math_init.js is a single-line ~727KB file using obfuscator.io-style string-array-shuffle obfuscation (rotator function on a large mixed hex/string table with a per-file decoder) and is unrelated to the package's advertised datetime-formatting purpose — the actual library body in dist/index.js is a small pure datetime formatter that has no runtime dependency on math_init.js. Fetching a separate JavaScript runtime specifically to execute a bundled obfuscated payload under it, rather than under Node, is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern designed to evade Node-based supply-chain scanners. The package name is in the @servicetitan scope but the behavior does not match a legitimate ServiceTitan datetime utility, consistent with a hijack or typosquat of that scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
